title: Morning eval rundown: KV cache + quant smoke
content:
2026-03-14 morning notes (quick, messy)

Goal: quick smoke + small evals to validate KV-cache interaction with quantized model variants and a prompt subset. Trying to reproduce the latency regression I saw yesterday on long prefixes.

Summary so far:
- Ran three smoke experiments across redwood-1-7b variants: fp16 baseline, q4_0, q2_k.
- Observed expected token throughput drop for q2_k on long-primed sequences (>=1024 context) and a small increase in first-token latency for q4_0 when KV cache is warmed.
- Prompt set: 60 short QA prompts (avg 18 tokens), 40 long-context prompts (avg 420 tokens).

Quick experiment log (commands paraphrased):
- exp-id: cass-0314-a | model: redwood-1-7b-fp16 | config: kv_cache=true, batch=8 | notes: baseline, warm-up 200 requests
  - median first-token latency: 42 ms
  - median tail-token latency: 9 ms/token
  - throughput: 320 tokens/s per GPU
  - quality: baseline references (BLEU ~N/A, prefer manual spot checks)

- exp-id: cass-0314-b | model: redwood-1-7b-q4_0 | config: kv_cache=true, batch=8
  - median first-token latency: 58 ms (↑ ~38% vs fp16)
  - tail-token: 8.3 ms/token (slightly better)
  - throughput: 345 tokens/s (surprising)
  - notes: observed tiny jitter on wifi but replicated on dedicated node; warm-up seemed to matter (cold start first 10 reqs were noisy)

- exp-id: cass-0314-c | model: redwood-1-7b-q2_k | config: kv_cache=true, batch=8
  - median first-token latency: 70 ms
  - tail-token: 12 ms/token (noticeable slowdown for long sequences)
  - throughput: 215 tokens/s
  - notes: seems quant kernel for q2_k struggles when KV-cache depth > 1024 (maybe cache layout or memory bandwidth?)

Probe: KV cache warm vs cold (same model q4_0):
- cold start first-token = 85 ms, after 50 warm requests = 58 ms (stabilizes around 55-60ms). Suggests compilation / JIT + cache filling matters.

Sample prompts (used subset for regression checks):
- Short QA: "What causes the seasons to change?"
- Long context: 2-paragraph customer email + "Summarize the ask and propose next steps." (used to stress KV cache)
- Prefix-only test: 1024 tokens of repeated phrase "Chapter 1:" then ask for continuation (to push KV address map)

Observations & hypotheses:
- q4_0 shows better token throughput despite higher first-token latency — maybe extra kernel path overhead at init but faster steady loops.
- q2_k prefers smaller contexts; look at memory access pattern: low-bit kernels can cause extra operations on cache reads for long sequences.
- There might be cross-talk between batching scheduler and KV-access when sequence length varies; observe spikes when mixing short+long in same batch (we batch by arrival, need to re-check grouping heuristics).

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Re-run cass-0314-b with batch grouping by sequence length (group small/long separately) — test if jitter goes away.
- [ ] Add perf counters for L2 cache misses on host (if available) during q2_k long runs.
- [ ] Create micro-bench: KV-only read loop across varying offsets (1..2048) to isolate kernel behavior.
- [ ] Drop into profiler (nv-nsight or similar) for q2_k long-run to capture memory copy patterns.
- [ ] Post a short note on #aml-kv in Slack with numbers + asking if anyone else saw q2_k long-context hit.

To-dos (medium):
- [ ] Draft a short PR with a toggle to group by context-length in the batcher (small patch, feature-flag behind experiment).
- [ ] Add a smoke CI job: run small prompt set on q4_0 and q2_k nightly and check median first-token latency + throughput regression thresholds.

Open questions / things to sanity-check:
- Is the first-token latency jump for q4_0 purely a JIT/compilation step? Need to capture kernel load times and any one-time allocations.
- For q2_k, are we hitting a pathological code-path in our quant kernel when copying KV slices (different code path for >1024)? Check code paths in kernel selection.
- Does the platform's auto-batching interact poorly when request length distribution is bimodal? Feels like it. Consider per-model batching policies.

Experiment commands & notes (copyable rough form):
- run_eval --model redwood-1-7b-q4_0 --prompts-file ./work/prompt_subset.json --batch-size 8 --kv-cache true --exp-name cass-0314-b --metrics first_token,per_token,throughput --warmup 200
- microkv --model redwood-1-7b-q2_k --max-offset 2048 --iters 500 --exp-name microkv-cass-0314

Logs & where to find data:
- perf traces: s3://redwood-telemetry/cassidy/2026-03-14/*.perf.gz
- raw eval outputs: s3://redwood-aml-results/cass-0314-*/
- quick csv summaries: /home/cassidy/tmp/cass-0314-summary.csv

Notes to self (informal):
- If I can't reproduce on dedicated node, maybe the earlier regression was noisy infra. But yesterday's customer report suggests production wide — so prioritize reproducing on dedicated and on-host.
- Keep the prompt set stable (commit prompt_subset.json before re-runs). Versioning the prompts (prompts/v1, v2) will help narrow flakiness.

Quick sketch of next-sprint items (for backlog):
- investigate kernel selection thresholds for q2_k (owner: Arjun)
- add per-model batching policy config to runtime (owner: Cassidy)
- add nightly smoke/regression for quant models (owner: Maya)

End crumb notes (random):
- Spotted weird log: "kv_cache_read: fallback to slow-path on shard 3" — capture exact timestamp and correlate to perf trace.
- Reminder: ping infra to reserve one dedicated 80GB A100 for a 3hr profiling window tomorrow morning (need stable infra).

-- Cassidy
